sentences.text: Researchers recorded activity from 1,415 neurons in neurosurgical patients who had just learned a story containing specific concepts.

Neurons associated with the learned concepts became active again during slow-wave sleep, firing together especially during sharp-wave ripples, a brief burst of high-frequency activity, with timing gaps that could support changes in synaptic connections.

The order in which these neurons reactivated did not match the sequence of concepts presented in the story, a pattern that contrasts with rodent place cells, which adjust their firing locations based on pre-existing sequences.
Unlike rodent place cells, human concept neurons are already tuned to specific meanings before any new learning occurs.
